title: build-inspector-nexus-graft
intention: GRAFT the build_inspector's LEARNING PATH to the question-nexus shape (charter filed edge (e), cast by the nexi-everywhere ruling, held-nexi-everywhere). The fire-path does not move: the FILTERS registry stays HARDWARE — the verdict is always hardware, replayable, changed only by installation (tooth 10's failure provenance + Akien's ratification), the tree never consulted at verdict-time. What grafts is the GROWTH: the inspector gains a tree stratum for its failure corpus (its own table, owner 'build_inspector', through the same generalized tools chart-tree proves), and when a failure would seed a filter, the proposal runs through the nexus loop — corpus walked, ceiling drafting the filter, admission through the unchanged gate. Its learnings COMPILE INTO the registry; a verdict never fires from the tree.
why: Akien, verbatim, 2026-07-28: 'building ANYTHING should be the learning event for the orient/inspector tickets.' The event the charter edge filed ('the first failure that would seed a filter') is REDEFINED and thereby FIRED: every journaled PROVEME exit runs this gate, so every build is a learning opportunity, and the stone cast today (chart-tree) is a build — the ticket casts now. The deeper why is the founding one made uniform: 'we find a new thing, we add a new filter' was always the nexus loop in prose; the graft makes it the one shared shape, with the candidate filters already seeded on edge (c) as the corpus's first questions.
traces_to: Law 1 — a failure class deposits once and compiles into a filter, and the class stops recurring; the ceiling is spent only on the novel proposal
Law 3 — the wrong-shape signal keeps its teeth: a second whole-repo sweep ever genuinely needed means the gate is not gating
Law 4 — admission stays physics: tooth 10 refuses a filter nobody was taught by; ratification stays Akien's (a gate learning its own leniency is the measured home-field risk)
Law 7 — a verdict is always hardware: replayable (same input + same registry revision = same verdict), which is what lets it be permanent in a record of truth
Law 8 — grafting one ticket at a time; falsifier (6) — an oracle or outbound import in inspector.py — keeps its teeth throughout

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate under the tester when built: the graft's teeth join test_inspector.py (or a sibling proof) — the fire-path teeth stay green untouched throughout; new teeth pin tree-never-at-verdict-time and admission-only-by-installation. Live gate: the first real failure that seeds a filter arrives through the loop, its provenance naming both the failure and the walk that drafted it — and the class stops recurring.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: a filter admitted without provenance naming the failure that taught it (tooth 10's claim, unchanged); the tree consulted at verdict-time (a live tree-walk verdict is not replayable); a fire-path tooth going red during the graft; the failure corpus written outside the inspector's own owned table (Law 6); the emit-chokepoint gate (transitions.py's five gate teeth) disturbed in any way — the wiring is settled, the graft touches only growth.
falsifier.horizon: re-read when chart-tree PROVES (the dependency clears); when the first failure lands through the loop; when edge (c)'s seeded candidates (stale-'on purpose' comments, host-seam seal expiry, charter-answers-how-it-learns) get their checkable shapes — each is a ready-made first walk for the corpus.
